s00: He's been shot, stabbed, set on fire, crushed by a TV and run over by a car, and somehow the phone still rings, because Ghostface was never just one guy. There have been sixteen different people behind that mask, so today we're ranking every single one of them, from the Ghostface you'd actually walk away from to the one you really, really don't want calling your house.
s01: Quick ground rules before we start. We're not ranking who's the coolest or whose movie was best, we're ranking how hard each one would be to survive, based on how many people they killed, how close they got to their victims, how smart the plan was, how strong they were and how hard they were to put down. And for every Ghostface you get one number, your survival rate. Unlike Michael or Jason, every one of these guys is human and every one of them ended up dead, so your odds are a lot better here, at least at the start.
s02: Number sixteen is Jason Carvey from Scream Six. He shows up in the opening, kills his film professor, and acts like he's the new face of the franchise, until he gets home and finds out the real Ghostface was waiting for him the whole time. He was the Ghostface for about five minutes before somebody scarier took the job. Survival rate: eighty-five percent. Instruction: check who's already in the apartment.
s03: Number fifteen is Karl Gibbs from Scream Seven. He's big and he's scary in a fight, but he's an escaped patient who was basically used as a pawn by the people really running things, and his run ends when Gale, Mindy and Chad hit him with a car. Survival rate: seventy-five percent. Instruction: stay near the people with the car keys.
s04: Number fourteen is Mrs. Loomis, Billy's mom, who spent the whole movie pretending to be a friendly reporter named Debbie Salt. Her plan was patient and honestly kind of brilliant, but up close she's the least dangerous fighter on this list, and once Cotton showed up with a gun, it was over. Survival rate: sixty-eight percent. Instruction: never trust a reporter who's a little too nice.
s05: Number thirteen is Charlie Walker, the horror nerd who knew every rule in the book. He pulled off a few kills, but the guy trusted the wrong partner, and Jill stabbed him through the heart the second she didn't need him anymore. Survival rate: sixty percent. Instruction: if he quizzes you on horror movies, leave.
s06: Number twelve is Quinn Bailey. She faked her own death so well that everyone stopped looking at her, which is a genuinely evil move, but she only got one confirmed kill before Sam shot her in the head. Survival rate: fifty-six percent. Instruction: see the body before you believe it.
s07: Number eleven is Ethan Landry, the awkward roommate who was always just a little too close. That closeness is exactly why he's dangerous, but in a straight fight he lost to Tara and then Kirby dropped a TV on his head, which is a very Scream way to go. Survival rate: fifty-three percent. Instruction: be suspicious of the nice roommate.
s08: Number ten is Marco Davis. He worked at the mental hospital and he was the tech guy behind the whole thing, faking calls and videos from Stu Macher with deepfakes, which is a terrifying idea, but when it came to the final fight, Sidney shot him. Survival rate: fifty percent. Instruction: if a dead killer calls you, it's not him.
s09: Number nine is Richie Kirsch, the sweet boyfriend nobody suspected for a single second. He stabbed the sheriff in broad daylight and fooled Sam the whole movie, but the moment she figured it out, she cut his throat and shot him to make sure. Survival rate: forty-five percent. Instruction: if your boyfriend loves horror movies a little too much, ask questions.
s10: Number eight is Jessica Bowden, Sidney's neighbor, and she was the one actually running everything in Scream Seven. She was willing to kill her own family to get what she wanted, which makes her colder than most people on this list, and it took Sidney and Tatum shooting together to stop her. Survival rate: forty-three percent. Instruction: know your neighbors better than they know you.
s11: Number seven is Stu Macher. A lot of fans would put him way higher, and he's easily one of the most unhinged Ghostfaces ever, but he only had a couple of kills, and Sidney ended him by dropping a TV right on his head. Stu might be one of the best Ghostfaces, but he's not the hardest to survive. Survival rate: forty percent. Instruction: keep a TV between you and him.
s12: Number six is Mickey Altieri, the film student who planned to get caught on purpose so he could blame the movies at his trial. He racked up one of the biggest body counts of the early films and even framed Derek, and when Gale and Sidney finally shot him, he still sat up one more time before they finished him off. Survival rate: thirty-six percent. Instruction: if he sits up, keep shooting.
s13: Number five is Amber Freeman, the best friend who killed Dewey. She got shot by Gale and fell into a burning stove, and she still came back out on fire, swinging a knife, and it took Tara shooting her in the head to end it. Survival rate: thirty percent. Instruction: if she's on fire and still walking, run.
s14: Number four is Billy Loomis, the original, the one who started all of this by killing Sidney's mom a year before the first movie even begins. He was her boyfriend, he planned everything and he played the victim perfectly, so he's probably everyone's favorite Ghostface, but he isn't the one you'd least want to meet, because three people on this list were even harder to survive. Survival rate: twenty-five percent. Instruction: if your boyfriend climbs through your window, check his pockets for a phone.
s15: Number three is Detective Wayne Bailey. He was the cop investigating the murders while he was committing them, which means the guy you'd call for help was the guy coming for you, and he led his whole family through the bloodiest run in Scream Six until Sam stabbed him in the eye. Survival rate: twenty-two percent. Instruction: don't call the detective on this case.
s16: Number two is Jill Roberts, Sidney's own cousin. She killed her friends, her mom and even her partner, then stabbed herself and smashed her own head into a frame to play the survivor, and she nearly got away with it before Sidney hit her with a defibrillator and shot her through the heart. Survival rate: eighteen percent. Instruction: if she's the last girl standing, look twice.
s17: And number one is Roman Bridger from Scream Three. He's Sidney's half-brother, he's the only Ghostface who ever worked completely alone, he has the most kills of anyone in the franchise, and he claims he's the one who pushed Billy into starting the original murders. He even wore a bulletproof vest, so shooting him in the chest did nothing, and it took a bullet to the head from Dewey to finally stop him. Survival rate: fifteen percent. Instruction: aim for the head, every time.
s18: So that's every Ghostface, from the guy who lasted five minutes to the one who planned it all. Tell me in the comments who you'd put at number one, and if you want Freddy or Pinhead next, you know where to ask.
